pr_title: Add template support to `issue create`, `pr create`
pr_body:
If multiple templates are found, the user is prompted to select one.

![gh issue template](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/887/71124795-eddafa80-21e5-11ea-9e8a-dd5245b6510c.gif)

The templates are searched for, in order of preference:

- issues:
  1. `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.md`
  2. `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md`
  3. `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.md`
  4. `ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md`
  5. `docs/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.md`
  6. `docs/ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md`

- pull requests:
  1. `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/*.md`
  2. `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
  3. `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/*.md`
  4. `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
  5. `docs/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/*.md`
  6. `docs/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`

The filename matches are case-insensitive.

**Not supported:** [organization-level default issue and pull request templates](https://help.github.com/en/github/building-a-strong-community/creating-a-default-community-health-file-for-your-organization). This feature only detects the templates found in the current repository.

Fixes #67

issue_context.title: Take templates into account for `pr create` and `issue create`
issue_context.body:
For `gh pr create` as far as I can tell, there aren't multiple templates to choose from so this will require just making sure the template is in the editor when you enter the description

For `gh issue create`, here's how I thought we could let you choose a template:

```
~/Projects/my-project$ gh issue create

Creating an issue in desktop/desktop

? Choose a template
> Bug report
  Feature request
  No template
? Title This is an issue title
? Body (nano) [Enter to launch editor]

_template in nano_

? Submit? 
> yes
  edit
  cancel

https://github.com/desktop/desktop/issues/4
```

review_comments: It's possible that I'm just too used to other languages but I find the use of `goto` here kind of jarring. I'm not sure it's one of my favorite Go features. I'd rather see the `goto`s replaced with a `return sortFn(results)`, I think, but I also can be convinced this is appropriate style.

Go's own stdlib uses `goto`; I found this explanation [in favor of goto quite compelling](https://stackoverflow.com/a/11065563/11687). I'm not opposed to using it when it increases readability, and Go's restrictions on how `goto` can be used (i.e. only within the same scope) ensures that we can't do anything too wild with it.

However, my main reason for using `goto` in this instance was to be able to `break` out of the outermost loop (as opposed to innermost one), so I'm going to replace my usage of `goto` with `break <label>`. 🙇
